name: task_create
description:
Create a bash-driven task card. The runtime polls `script` every `check_interval` seconds while the card is pending. The LAST line of stdout decides what happens:

  * `[skip]`             — not yet; check again next interval
  * `[start]`            — wake the agent now
  * `[start] <message>`  — wake the agent; `<message>` becomes the seed input shown in the wakeup
  * `[done]`             — mark the card finished WITHOUT waking the agent (script-level finalisation; same effect as the agent calling `task_finish` from inside a wakeup)

Non-zero exit / unrecognised output is fail-closed (treated as `[skip]` and logged as `task_check_error`).

Examples — just the `script` body:
  * Every hour: `echo [start]` (check_interval=3600)
  * After 9am daily: `[[ $(date +%H) -ge 9 ]] && echo [start] || echo [skip]`
  * When a build flag appears: `[[ -f build/done.flag ]] && echo "[start] build ready" || echo [skip]`
  * Self-retiring after a deadline: `(( $(date +%s) >= 1735689600 )) && echo [done] || echo [start]`

The script lands on disk at core/tasks/<name>.sh; you can edit it later with bash or via `task_update`.

name.description: Task name (unique per session; used as the filename under core/tasks/).

description.description: What this task should do when it fires. Shown in the wakeup prompt.

check_interval.description: Seconds between script runs. Defaults to 3600 (1h).

script.description: Bash snippet (body only — shebang is prepended). Last line of stdout MUST be `[skip]`, `[start]`, `[start] <message>`, or `[done]`.
